reason: the design fails 4 of its checks

findings.text: RQCLA-13 is not covered: No SPEC tests that `claim_coordinator_release` specifically removes `zbuild:claimed`; DSCLA-5 (Other SPEC, claims coverage) tests only the end state — label absent after normal completion — but would pass even if the removal was done by runner.sh calling gh directly, bypassing the coordinator's hook; no SPEC analogous to DSCLA-18 exists that calls `claim_coordinator_release` and asserts it removes the label via `gh issue edit` — The coordinator's release hook removes the `zbuild:claimed` label [FIX IN DESIGN: add or widen a SPEC so it covers this]

RQARC-1 is not covered: DSCLA-18 tests only that `claim_coordinator_claim` adds `zbuild:claimed` via `gh issue edit`; no SPEC tests the other half — that `claim_coordinator_release` (also in `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/`) removes `zbuild:claimed` via `gh issue edit`; DSCLA-5/6/7/13 test only that the label is absent after various exit paths, not that the removal call is in the plugin — The label calls (`gh issue edit`) are in `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/` [FIX IN DESIGN: add or widen a SPEC so it covers this]

RQARC-2 is not covered: DSCLA-19 tests only that `zbuild_claim_acquire` contains no direct `gh` calls; `zbuild_claim_release` in `core/claim/claim.sh` is equally "under core/" and no SPEC tests it contains no direct `gh` calls; DSCLA-17 (Other SPEC) tests the no-op guard path (no prior acquire) but not that a live release delegates to the coordinator without a direct `gh` call — Nothing under `core/` calls `gh` for the label [FIX IN DESIGN: add or widen a SPEC so it covers this]

Steps: a step no requirement needs: No requirement names `config/shape-change-paths.txt` or asks that future changes to `core/claim/claim.sh` trigger a shape floor; this step is an internal engineering choice outside the issue's scope — Add core/claim/claim.sh to config/shape-change-paths.txt so future changes to the claim bridge trigger the shape floor [FIX IN DESIGN: take the step out, or make it what a requirement asks]

answers: design finding 1: done — Redesigned `claim.sh` to call the public hooks `claim_coordinator_claim` and `claim_coordinator_release` instead of `_ccgl_*` internals. `claim_coordinator_claim` is now amended (in the plugin.sh step) to return `{"acquired": false, "holder": "<extracted_holder>"}` on conflict, so `claim.sh` parses the JSON output. The step for `plugin.sh` explicitly removes the `source` of `core/claim/claim.sh` currently at plugin.sh lines 251-260 (the circular dependency from the previous implementation). The dependency arrow is strictly: `runner.sh` → `claim.sh` → `plugin.sh`.

design finding 2: done — Changed `DSCLA-18` from `[no-code]` to `[code]` and added Given/When/Then. Test fails on base code because `claim_coordinator_claim` adds `claimed:<machine>` (not `zbuild:claimed`); passes after.

design finding 3: done — Changed `DSCLA-19` from `[no-code]` to `[code]` and added Given/When/Then. Test fails on base code because `core/claim/claim.sh` does not exist; passes after the file is created.

design finding 4: done — Restructured the Decision section so each major component is a single bold bullet with concise, self-contained description. Removed the multi-line "Startup process budget" prose paragraph (not a decision) and the complex multi-line `claim.sh` paragraph that embedded `_ccgl_*` function names. The amended `claim.sh` decision bullet now cleanly states it calls `claim_coordinator_claim` and `claim_coordinator_release`, matching the step text verbatim.
